CISA.MS.AAD.2.1.title: Users detected as high risk SHALL be blocked.

CISA.MS.AAD.2.2.title: A notification SHOULD be sent to the administrator when high-risk users are detected.

CISA.MS.AAD.2.3.title: Sign-ins detected as high risk SHALL be blocked.

CISA.MS.AAD.3.1.title: Phishing-resistant MFA SHALL be enforced for all users.

CISA.MS.AAD.3.2.title: If phishing-resistant MFA has not been enforced, an alternative MFA method SHALL be enforced for all users.

CISA.MS.AAD.3.3.title: If Microsoft Authenticator is enabled, it SHALL be configured to show login context information.

CISA.MS.AAD.3.4.title: The Authentication Methods Manage Migration feature SHALL be set to Migration Complete.

CISA.MS.AAD.3.5.title: The authentication methods SMS, Voice Call, and Email One-Time Passcode (OTP) SHALL be disabled.

CISA.MS.AAD.3.6.title: Phishing-resistant MFA SHALL be required for highly privileged roles.

CISA.MS.AAD.3.7.title: Managed devices SHOULD be required for authentication.

CISA.MS.AAD.3.8.title: Managed Devices SHOULD be required to register MFA.

CISA.MS.AAD.4.1.title: Security logs SHALL be sent to the agency's security operations center for monitoring.

CISA.MS.AAD.5.1.title: Only administrators SHALL be allowed to register applications.

CISA.MS.AAD.5.2.title: Only administrators SHALL be allowed to consent to applications.

CISA.MS.AAD.5.3.title: An admin consent workflow SHALL be configured for applications.

CISA.MS.AAD.5.4.title: Group owners SHALL NOT be allowed to consent to applications.

CISA.MS.AAD.7.1.title: A minimum of two users and a maximum of eight users SHALL be provisioned with the Global Administrator role.

CISA.MS.AAD.7.2.title: Privileged users SHALL be provisioned with finer-grained roles instead of Global Administrator.

CISA.MS.AAD.7.3.title: Privileged users SHALL be provisioned cloud-only accounts separate from an on-premises directory or other federated identity providers.

CISA.MS.AAD.7.4.title: Permanent active role assignments SHALL NOT be allowed for highly privileged roles.

CISA.MS.AAD.7.5.title: Provisioning users to highly privileged roles SHALL NOT occur outside of a PAM system.

CISA.MS.AAD.7.6.title: Activation of the Global Administrator role SHALL require approval.

CISA.MS.AAD.7.7.title: Eligible and Active highly privileged role assignments SHALL trigger an alert.

CISA.MS.AAD.7.8.title: User activation of the Global Administrator role SHALL trigger an alert.

CISA.MS.AAD.7.9.title: User activation of other highly privileged roles SHOULD trigger an alert.

CISA.MS.AAD.8.1.title: Guest users SHOULD have limited or restricted access to Azure AD directory objects.

CISA.MS.AAD.8.2.title: Only users with the Guest Inviter role SHOULD be able to invite guest users.

CISA.MS.AAD.8.3.title: Guest invites SHOULD only be allowed to specific external domains that have been authorized by the agency for legitimate business purposes.

CISA.MS.EXO.1.1.title: Automatic forwarding to external domains SHALL be disabled.

CISA.MS.EXO.2.1.title: A list of approved IP addresses for sending mail SHALL be maintained.

CISA.MS.EXO.2.2.title: An SPF policy SHALL be published for each domain, designating only these addresses as approved senders.

CISA.MS.EXO.3.1.title: DKIM SHOULD be enabled for all domains.

CISA.MS.EXO.4.1.title: A DMARC policy SHALL be published for every second-level domain.

CISA.MS.EXO.4.2.title: The DMARC message rejection option SHALL be p=reject.

CISA.MS.EXO.4.3.title: The DMARC point of contact for aggregate reports SHALL include reports@dmarc.cyber.dhs.gov.

CISA.MS.EXO.6.1.title: Contact folders SHALL NOT be shared with all domains.

CISA.MS.EXO.6.2.title: Calendar details SHALL NOT be shared with all domains.

CISA.MS.EXO.7.1.title: External sender warnings SHALL be implemented.

CISA.MS.EXO.8.1.title: A DLP solution SHALL be used.

CISA.MS.EXO.8.2.title: The DLP solution SHALL protect personally identifiable information (PII) and sensitive information, as defined by the agency.

CISA.MS.EXO.8.3.title: The selected DLP solution SHOULD offer services comparable to the native DLP solution offered by Microsoft.

CISA.MS.EXO.8.4.title: At a minimum, the DLP solution SHALL restrict sharing credit card numbers, U.S. Individual Taxpayer Identification Numbers (ITIN), and U.S. Social Security numbers (SSN) via email.

CISA.MS.EXO.9.1.title: Emails SHALL be filtered by attachment file types.

CISA.MS.EXO.9.2.title: The attachment filter SHOULD attempt to determine the true file type and assess the file extension.

CISA.MS.EXO.9.3.title: Disallowed file types SHALL be determined and enforced.

CISA.MS.EXO.9.4.title: Alternatively chosen filtering solutions SHOULD offer services comparable to Microsoft Defender's Common Attachment Filter.

CISA.MS.EXO.9.5.title: At a minimum, click-to-run files SHOULD be blocked (e.g., .exe, .cmd, and .vbe).

CISA.MS.EXO.10.1.title: Emails SHALL be scanned for malware.

CISA.MS.EXO.10.2.title: Emails identified as containing malware SHALL be quarantined or dropped.

CISA.MS.EXO.10.3.title: Email scanning SHALL be capable of reviewing emails after delivery.

CISA.MS.EXO.11.1.title: Impersonation protection checks SHOULD be used.

CISA.MS.EXO.11.2.title: User warnings, comparable to the user safety tips included with EOP, SHOULD be displayed.

CISA.MS.EXO.11.3.title: The phishing protection solution SHOULD include an AI-based phishing detection tool comparable to EOP Mailbox Intelligence.

CISA.MS.EXO.12.1.title: IP allow lists SHOULD NOT be created.

CISA.MS.EXO.12.2.title: Safe lists SHOULD NOT be enabled.

CISA.MS.EXO.14.1.title: A spam filter SHALL be enabled.

CISA.MS.EXO.14.2.title: Spam and high confidence spam SHALL be moved to either the junk email folder or the quarantine folder.

CISA.MS.EXO.14.3.title: Allowed domains SHALL NOT be added to inbound anti-spam protection policies.

CISA.MS.EXO.14.4.title: If a third-party party filtering solution is used, the solution SHOULD offer services comparable to the native spam filtering offered by Microsoft.

CISA.MS.EXO.15.1.title: URL comparison with a block-list SHOULD be enabled.

CISA.MS.EXO.15.2.title: Direct download links SHOULD be scanned for malware.

CISA.MS.EXO.15.3.title: User click tracking SHOULD be enabled.

CISA.MS.EXO.16.2.title: Alerts SHOULD be sent to a monitored address or incorporated into a security information and event management (SIEM) system.

CISA.MS.EXO.17.1.title: Microsoft Purview Audit (Standard) logging SHALL be enabled.

CISA.MS.EXO.17.2.title: Microsoft Purview Audit (Premium) logging SHALL be enabled.

CISA.MS.EXO.17.3.title: Audit logs SHALL be maintained for at least the minimum duration dictated by OMB M-21-31 (Appendix C).

CISA.MS.SHAREPOINT.1.1.title: External sharing for SharePoint SHALL be limited to Existing guests or Only People in your organization.

CISA.MS.SHAREPOINT.1.2.title: External sharing for OneDrive SHALL be limited to Existing guests or Only People in your organization.

CISA.MS.SHAREPOINT.1.3.title: External sharing SHALL be restricted to approved external domains and/or users in approved security groups per interagency collaboration needs.

CISA.MS.SHAREPOINT.2.1.title: File and folder default sharing scope SHALL be set to Specific People.

CISA.MS.SHAREPOINT.2.2.title: File and folder default sharing permissions SHALL be set to View only.

CISA.MS.SHAREPOINT.3.1.title: Expiration days for Anyone links SHALL be set to 30 days or less.

CISA.MS.SHAREPOINT.3.2.title: Allowable file and folder permissions for Anyone links SHALL be set to View only.

CISA.MS.SHAREPOINT.3.3.title: Reauthentication days for people who use a verification code SHALL be set to 30 days or less.
